title: Living or Non-living?
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.6-7, Worksheet Q1

scenes.t: Yahia is a young scientist. Today he asks a big question: how can we tell if something is living or non-living?
Meet MRS GREN! She is living, because she can do the seven life processes. Each letter of her name is one process.
M is for Movement: she can move from one place to another. R is for Respiration: she breathes in oxygen to get energy.
S is for Sensitivity: she can feel pain, sound, heat, cold and light. G is for Growth: she gets bigger, like a child becomes an adult.
R is for Reproduction: she can have babies. E is for Excretion: she gets rid of wastes from her body.
N is for Nutrition: she needs food and water to live. All living things, like animals and plants, do these seven things.
Non-living things, like plastic, stone, air, water and the sun, do not eat, breathe, sense, grow or reproduce.
Some non-living things can move, like fans, clocks and cars. But they move with electricity or gas, not by themselves!

activities.title: Living, Non-living or Dead?
activities.prompt: Catch the word and send it to the right group!

activities.title: Grow a Bean
activities.goal: Prove a bean seed is living: watch it grow!

predict.q: What will happen to the bean in a few days?
o: It will grow roots and a shoot

steps.t: Put wet cotton wool inside the clear cup.
Push the beans between the cotton and the side of the cup so you can see them.
Add a little water every day. Keep the cotton wet, not flooded.
Put the cup near a window and look at it every day for one week.

activities.result: After a few days the bean grows a root, then a green shoot. It gets bigger every day!
activities.why: Growth and nutrition are life processes. The bean uses water to grow, so it is a living thing.
